core_concept: CSS selectors are fundamental for targeting specific HTML elements to apply styles. They allow developers to use various methods like ID selectors (using '#') and class selectors (using '.') to precisely control the appearance of web pages. Understanding selector chaining and grouping techniques further enhances styling capabilities, promoting efficient and maintainable code.
technical_breakdown: ID selectors target elements based on their unique `id` attribute.
Class selectors target elements with a specific `class` attribute.
Selector chaining allows combining class and ID selectors for more granular targeting.
Grouping selectors reduce code repetition by applying the same styles to multiple classes simultaneously.
